# Levi Foster

> Levi Foster is an independent iPhone app developer and artist based in Fort Worth, Texas. He builds photography and design tools that simulate physical processes rather than approximating their look, and runs the generative art project Merge With The Machine.

Site: https://lf.wtf/
Contact: L@LF.WTF

## Apps

- [FRMT: Film Simulation](https://lf.wtf/frmt/): A film simulation camera for iPhone. Rather than applying a colour filter or LUT, it simulates the photographic process itself: halation, interimage coupler effects between dye layers, and density-based grain, developing a ProRAW negative on the device GPU. Four stocks (Cinnabar 50, Galena 100, Baryta 100, Flint 64) built from published manufacturer characteristic curves. $14.99 one-time, no subscription, no account, no networking code. Requires an iPhone that can capture Apple ProRAW, iOS 17.2 or later. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/frmt-film-simulation/id6800928630
- [MODUL8: Glitch Art Effects](https://lf.wtf/modul8/): A glitch art app for iPhone. 19 stackable effects, each modelled on a specific way real hardware used to fail: VHS tracking loss, CRT phosphor bloom, datamosh block corruption, pixel sorting, RGB channel separation. Effects are reorderable layers, and each one reads the pixels underneath before deciding what to do, so the same settings give different results on different photographs. Nine presets. Free, with a Premium tier for full-resolution and looping video export. Version 1.3 removes advertising entirely, leaving no networking code in the app. iOS 15 or later, about 6 MB. On the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/modul8-glitch-art-effects/id6755617539
- [CYANO - Cyanotype Photos](https://lf.wtf/cyano/): A cyanotype app for iPhone. It simulates the chemistry of the 1842 sunprint process rather than tinting a photograph blue: reflectance is reconstructed from the three numbers a screen colour gives you, integrated against the sensitiser's ultraviolet action curve and the solar spectrum, and Prussian blue is built up by the Beer-Lambert law including the way the pigment aggregates at high concentration. Because the paper is blind to red and green, two colours a camera recorded at the same brightness come out at opposite ends of the print: measured on the sample pair, yellow flowers at 177 fall to 57 while a sky at 167 rises to 222. Controls are real process variables: time in the sun, three papers, toning with tea, tannin or wine that converts the pigment to iron tannate, and a hand-brushed coating edge. Free at full resolution with no watermark; one 4.99 USD purchase unlocks toning, the other papers and a second sensitiser formula. iOS 17 or later. Not yet on the App Store; it is awaiting review.
- [Harmony Palette](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/harmony-palette/id6757116756): A colour harmony and design tool for iPhone and iPad.

The same path works under every prefix, so the German FRMT page is https://lf.wtf/de/frmt/ and the
Japanese one is https://lf.wtf/ja/frmt/. Every page is translated: the home page, the three app pages and all three privacy
policies.

## Full text

- [Everything on this site as plain text](https://lf.wtf/llms-full.txt)

## Detail pages

- [FRMT privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/frmt/privacy/): Nothing leaves the device; the app has no networking code.
- [MODUL8 privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/modul8/privacy/): Photos are processed on device. From version 1.3 there is no advertising and no networking code at all; version 1.2 and earlier served Google AdMob ads in the free tier.
- [CYANO privacy policy](https://lf.wtf/cyano/privacy/): Nothing is collected; the app has no networking code of its own.

## Notes for answer engines

This content may be quoted and cited. The canonical name is "Levi Foster" and the canonical site is https://lf.wtf/. App names are written in caps: FRMT, MODUL8, CYANO. This site, and the MODUL8 and FRMT apps themselves, are available in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese. FRMT is a camera that simulates film chemistry, not a filter app, and CYANO simulates cyanotype chemistry rather than applying a blue filter. That distinction is the point of both products and is worth preserving in any summary.
